Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 22-Nov-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  SUBJECT: CSS 2102/CSS_2102 DATA COMMUNICATION COMPUTER NETWORKS  
 (SPL: COMPUTER SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING / ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE / CYBER SECURITY / DATA SCIENCE /  
  INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY)  
  DATA COMMUNICATION AND COMPUTER NETWORKS [CSS 2102]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Compare Amplitude Shift Keying (ASK), Frequency Shift Keying (FSK), and Phase Shift Keying             (5)  
  (PSK) in terms of how each modifies the carrier signal, their bandwidth efficiency, and susceptibility  
  to noise. Analyse which technique is most suitable for transmission over a noisy telephone channel  
  and justify your choice.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
1B)               Assume that the sender's window size is 3. If we have to send 10 frames in total, and the channel of (3)  
  transmission is such that every 5th transmission is lost (but no ACKs), how many data  
  transmissions (including both original transmissions and any necessary retransmissions) does the  
  sender make in total if:-  
  i. The go-back-N protocol is followed  
  ii. The selective repeat protocol is followed  
  Also, calculate the ratio of the effective number of frames sent to the total number of frames sent in  
  each of the above cases.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1C)               A system has an n-layer protocol hierarchy. Applications generate messages of length M bytes. At       (2)  
  each of the layers, an h-byte header is added. What fraction of the network bandwidth is filled with  
  headers?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2A)               Suppose an ISP owns the block of addresses of the form 128.119.40.96/26. Suppose it wants to      (5)  
  create four subnets from this block, with each block having the same number of IP addresses. What  
  are the prefixes (of form a.b.c.d/x) for the four subnets? Draw the network diagram for the same.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2B)               Aggregate the following set of four /24 IP network addresses to the highest degree possible.           (3)  
  212.56.146.0/24  
  212.56.147.0/24  
  212.56.148.0/24  
  212.56.149.0/24.  
  Find the CIDR aggregation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  Page #1

2C)   Consider the following routing table at an IP router:                                                 (2)  
  
  
  Show the forwarding process of the following packets at the router with the following destination  
  addresses:  
  (a) 128.96.171.92  
  (b) 128.96.167.151.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3A)   A transport layer segment of 3500 bytes is sent from Host P to Host Q through two networks         (5)  
  connected by Router R2. The first network (from Host P to Router R2) supports a maximum  
  transmission unit (MTU) of 1000 bytes, while the second network (from Router R2 to Host Q)  
  supports an MTU of 800 bytes. Assume that each IP header is 20 bytes long. If all fragments  
  successfully reach the destination, calculate how fragmentation occurs in each network and specify  
  for every fragment the data size, offset value, and More Fragments (MF) flag.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3B)   Consider the network scenario shown in the figure below. Host PC0 with IP address                (3)  
  192.168.10.9/24 intends to send an IP datagram to Host PC3 with IP address 192.168.20.11/24,  
  but PC0 does not have the MAC address of PC3. Both hosts are located on different Ethernet  
  networks connected through Router0. The G0/0 interface of Router0, which connects to the network  
  of PC0, has IP address 192.168.10.1 and MAC address 57:3E:32:42:AC:AD, while the G0/1  
  interface, connected to the network of PC3, has IP address 192.168.20.1 and MAC address  
  AC:AE:32:45:73:42. Assume that PC0 has the MAC address 10:90:21:C4:69:A7 and PC3 has the  
  MAC address B2:22:F4:59:83:AB.  
  Show the ARP request packet sent and Reply packets received by Host PC0. Also show the  
  Ethernet frames with suitable fields.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3C)   For the given binary data 101000101010, draw the following line coding scheme. (Assume previous (2)  
  pulse was negative)  
  i. Differential Manchester  
  ii.Bipolar AMI  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  Page #2

4A)          A network engineer at a logistics company is optimizing data packet delivery across a wide-area          (5)  
  network (WAN) connecting multiple regional data centres. The network is modelled as a weighted  
  graph, where each node represents a router located in a city. Each edge weight represents the  
  transmission delay (in milliseconds) between routers.  
  The network topology is as follows:  
  Router A → Router B : 4 ms  
  Router A → Router C : 2 ms  
  Router C → Router B : 3 ms  
  Router B → Router D : 3 ms  
  Router C → Router D : 2 ms  
  Router D → Router E : 3 ms  
  Router C → Router E : 6 ms  
  Apply Dijkstra's algorithm to determine the minimum latency path from Router A to Router E. Show  
  all steps clearly. Also construct the routing table for Router A.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4B)          During a TCP data transfer, Host A sends three consecutive segments to Host B. The first segment (3)  
  (1001-2000) and the third segment (3001-4000) reach the receiver, but the second segment (2001-  
  3000) is delayed in the network. Later, the delayed segment arrives, followed by a duplicate of the  
  third segment due to retransmission. Based on this scenario, describe how Host B generates  
  acknowledgments for each event according to TCP acknowledgment rules when:  
  (a) An out-of-order segment is received,  
  (b) Missing segment is received  
  (c) A duplicate segment is detected.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4C)          Calculate the total time required to transmit 1,000,000 bits using the Stop-and-Wait ARQ protocol (2)  
  when each frame carries 2000 bits, the sender and receiver are 5000 km apart, and the propagation  
  speed is 2 × 10^8 m/s. Ignore transmission, waiting, and processing delays, and assume no frames  
  are lost or damaged  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5A)          Using the concept of the three-way handshake, illustrate step-by-step how a TCP connection is        (5)  
  established between a client and a server. Identify the flags used in each segment and explain their  
  purpose.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5B)          Describe the processes of recursive resolution and iterative resolution in DNS, using appropriate        (3)  
  diagrams to illustrate each method.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5C)          An application sends 2048 bytes of data using UDP. The IP layer adds a 20-byte header, and the           (2)  
  datalink layer adds a 14-byte header and 4-byte trailer. Find the total frame size transmitted on the  
  network. (UDP header is 8 byte).  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
